firstPlayer: the player whose marker starts on top
turnCap: none needed: every action moves a marker at least 1 toward 60
agreementCountedOn: Expert decisions with 2+ sensible options, all Expert games

sanity.position: lethal: he is at 3, my Raider is ready, his Quick 2/1 tempts a free kill: attack him
free trade: my ready Heavy 5/6 against his ready Quick 2/1 (his only card), I am at 2 and he acts next: attack the Quick
don't waste: Hit 3 and Hit 6 in hand, his Quick 2/1 and Heavy 5/6: never Hit 6 the Quick
don't waste: Haste in hand, my Line already ready: never Haste it

report.summary: Every machine criterion passes. Expert (determinized information-set MCTS, 3000 play-outs a decision in the gate, 5000 on the page, play-outs to the end of the game) beats Random 100%, Greedy 93.8%, Racer 79.3% over 400 games each; set positions 5/5 on all four (Greedy fails lethal); no caps possible; Expert equals Greedy in 34.9% of 24,594 decisions; the player whose marker starts on top wins 50.4% of Expert mirrors. Mirror games are short, about 25 actions, and end on life almost always (6 of 400 reached 60/60). The Racer is the only trivial bot that holds Expert near the line.
report.loop: On each action you choose what to spend time on: a unit (its time, plus 3 before it can swing), a removal Hit, an attack (1 time) or a draw (2 time). Expert mostly sends units at the opponent's life and spends Hits on the opponent's biggest units rather than at life; unit-on-unit trades are rare (2 of 11 attacks in a typical mirror). The best play boils down to: get damage-per-time onto the board early, kill the opponent's big converters with Hits, and draw when no action buys more than 2 time's worth. Because whoever is behind acts, a big card (Slow, 9 time) hands the opponent a run of consecutive actions, which is the real price of a big card.
report.notes: The spec's free-trade position (Heavy against a Quick in an even game) does not discriminate: self-play from it wins 97% whether the Heavy hits the Quick or the face, so it was replaced by one where the trade is the only move that does not lose. The rules add a Wait (time 1) for the rare case where nothing is legal; the spec had none.
